frames.narration: A shopper uploads a photo and asks for similar items that are in stock. The app sends the photo to the embedding service, which returns a vector of 768 numbers made by the current model, version 3.
The query API asks the filter planner how selective 'in stock' is. The attribute index estimates that 40% of the 100 million items match, which is too many for exact distances to each one.

states.planner: search the graph, filter while walking

frames.narration: So the plan is to search the graph. The query goes to all 8 shards in parallel, each with a bitmap of the items in stock. A shard walks its graph with compressed distances and skips vectors that do not match.
Each shard holds 12.5 million vectors, so it finds its candidates in about 3 ms. The few hundred best candidates are then reranked with exact distances, using the full vectors that are read from SSD.

Every shard returns its 10 best with their distances. The API merges the 80 results and keeps the 10 smallest distances. Anything in the global top 10 is in the top 10 of its own shard, so the merge is exact for what the shards found. The whole search took 9 ms.
Meanwhile a seller deletes an item. The write goes to the update log first, so it is durable. The shard that owns the id marks it with a tombstone, and searches hide it within a second or two.
Later a background merge rebuilds the segment without the deleted vectors and swaps in the new index. The tombstone is gone and the space comes back. The search path never stopped.
